nrIncident.summary: Disruption in the Barking area until at least the end of the day on Tuesday 27 October: amended Suffragette line service, and no trains between Barking and Grays via Rainham (Essex)
nrIncident.routes:
c2c through Barking
London Overground between Gospel Oak and Barking Riverside
nrIncident.message:
A freight train has derailed between Woodgrange Park and Barking, blocking some lines.
Some trains through Barking will be cancelled or revised as a result. Where trains do run there may be delays of up to 10 minutes in the area.
• London Overground are running a reduced half hourly service on the Suffragette line between Gospel Oak and Woodgrange Park. No trains will run between Woodgrange Park and Barking Riverside
• There will be no c2c service between Barking and Grays via Dagenham Dock, Rainham (Essex) and Purfleet
• c2c services that run to / from London Liverpool Street will instead to be diverted to / from London Fenchurch Street - please be aware that there has been a late notice change to the engineering work that was scheduled to take place between London Fenchurch Street and Barking
Disruption is expected until at least the end of the day on Tuesday 27 October.
A visual disruption map video is available.
c2c customer advice:
What's happened?
A freight train has derailed between Woodgrange Park and Barking, which means platforms 7 and 8 at Barking station are blocked.
How does this affect my journey?
No services are calling at Dagenham Dock, Rainham or Purfleet. Please expect delays and service alterations.
Services to / from London Liverpool Street via Stratford (London) will instead run to / from London Fenchurch Street via West Ham. London Liverpool Street and London Fenchurch Street are a short distance apart.
Your ticket will be accepted at no extra cost on:
• First Essex buses between Purfleet and Grays
• Greater Anglia between London Liverpool Street and Southend Victoria
• London Buses between Barking, Dagenham Dock, Rainham, Purfleet and Grays
• London Buses Superloop SL12
• London Buses EL2 for Dagenham Dock
• London Underground District line between Barking and Upminster, and Jubilee line between West Ham and Stratford (London)
Replacement buses are running half hourly between between Upminster and Grays, calling at Rainham, Purfleet, Grays.
What should I do?
Please check before you travel and allow extra time for your journey. c2c are working to keep customers moving and will provide details of any alternative travel arrangements as soon as they are confirmed.
London Overground customer advice:
Service is suspended between Woodgrange Park and Barking Riverside.
Your ticket can be used, at no extra cost, on London Buses via any reasonable route in order to complete your journey.
Information for customers travelling Monday 26 October
A half hourly service will operate between Gospel Oak and South Tottenham. Services between South Tottenham and Barking Riverside will be part suspended.

If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.

nrIncident.message:

There may be further changes to service levels across the LNER network depending on the impact of Storm Boelo.
Today, Sunday 25 October you are advised not to travel between Edinburgh and Aberdeen in either direction due to expected disruption.
Across the rest of the LNER network, you are strongly encouraged to check your journey before travelling and allow extra time where possible.
Service impact:
Current disruptions:
Bradford Forster Square - until the end of the day
Due to severe weather on the Leeds to Bradford Forster Square route, Northern have had to cancel all their services on that route for the rest of the day.
As a result of this, there is no platform availability at Bradford Forster Square.
LNER services to / from Bradford Forster Square will be revised to terminate and start back from Leeds.
Northallerton - Edinburgh - until the end of the day
Speed restrictions between Northallerton and Edinburgh means that trains have to run at reduced speed on all lines. As a result of this, trains running between these stations may be delayed.
Your ticket can be used at no extra cost on TransPennine Express, CrossCountry and alternative LNER services.
Please note that other train operators are affected by this disruption.
Today, Sunday 25 October
• Trains are expected to run normally between London Kings Cross and Doncaster / Leeds
• A reduced service of one train per hour is running between Northallerton / Darlington and Newcastle / Edinburgh, with short notice delays and alterations also possible
• Trains between Northallerton and Edinburgh will run at reduced speeds, extending journey times
• All LNER services to and from Aberdeen, with the exception of the 13:47 Aberdeen to Edinburgh service, will be cancelled
• LNER services will continue running to and from Inverness, with short notice delays possible
Due to the severity of the weather and expected road closures, rail replacement coaches will not be available between Edinburgh and Aberdeen. As other operators are also impacted, it will not be possible to travel with a different train company.
Ticket easements:
Customers are advised not to travel between Edinburgh and Aberdeen in either direction due to expected disruption. nrIncident.summary: Storm Boelo - disruption to TransPennine Express services until 06:00
nrIncident.routes: Various routes across the TransPennine Express network
nrIncident.message:
Following storm Boelo which brough disruption on various routes on the TransPennine Express network, residual disruption may still be in place on multiple lines.
Ticket easements and refunds:
If you have a ticket dated for travel on Sunday 25 October, you can use it on any TransPennine Express service on Monday 26 or Tuesday 27 October at no extra cost. You do not need to buy a new ticket.
Customers with tickets dated today, Sunday 25 October, arrangements have been made for you to use your ticket to travel on the limited Avanti West Coast services that are running on Sunday between Preston, Carlisle and Edinburgh / Glasgow at no extra cost and Avanti West Coast customers can also use their tickets to travel on TransPennine Express services between these destinations (where applicable). Please bear in mind the services that do run may be delayed or cancelled at short notice and you may experience overcrowding.
If your intended train is cancelled or you’re unable to complete your journey, you can apply for a refund from the retailer you purchased your ticket from.
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.

nrIncident.summary: Disruption in the Barking area until at least the end of the day on Tuesday 27 October: amended Suffragette line service, and no trains between Barking and Grays via Rainham (Essex)
nrIncident.routes:
c2c through Barking
London Overground between Gospel Oak and Barking Riverside
nrIncident.message:
A freight train has derailed between Woodgrange Park and Barking, blocking some lines.
Some trains through Barking will be cancelled or revised as a result. Where trains do run there may be delays of up to 10 minutes in the area.
• London Overground are running a reduced half hourly service on the Suffragette line between Gospel Oak and Woodgrange Park. No trains will run between Woodgrange Park and Barking Riverside
• There will be no c2c service between Barking and Grays via Dagenham Dock, Rainham (Essex) and Purfleet
• c2c services that run to / from London Liverpool Street will instead to be diverted to / from London Fenchurch Street - please be aware that there has been a late notice change to the engineering work that was scheduled to take place between London Fenchurch Street and Barking
Disruption is expected until at least the end of the day on Tuesday 27 October.
A visual disruption map video is available.
c2c customer advice:
What's happened?
A freight train has derailed between Woodgrange Park and Barking, which means platforms 7 and 8 at Barking station are blocked.
How does this affect my journey?
No services are calling at Dagenham Dock, Rainham or Purfleet. Please expect delays and service alterations.
Services to / from London Liverpool Street via Stratford (London) will instead run to / from London Fenchurch Street via West Ham. London Liverpool Street and London Fenchurch Street are a short distance apart.
Your ticket will be accepted at no extra cost on:
• First Essex buses between Purfleet and Grays
• Greater Anglia between London Liverpool Street and Southend Victoria
• London Buses between Barking, Dagenham Dock, Rainham, Purfleet and Grays
• London Buses Superloop SL12
• London Buses EL2 for Dagenham Dock
• London Underground District line between Barking and Upminster, and Jubilee line between West Ham and Stratford (London)
Replacement buses are running half hourly between between Upminster and Grays, calling at Rainham, Purfleet, Grays.
What should I do?
Please check before you travel and allow extra time for your journey. c2c are working to keep customers moving and will provide details of any alternative travel arrangements as soon as they are confirmed.
London Overground customer advice:
Service is suspended between Woodgrange Park and Barking Riverside.
Your ticket can be used, at no extra cost, on London Buses via any reasonable route in order to complete your journey.
Information for customers travelling Monday 26 October
A half hourly service will operate between Gospel Oak and South Tottenham. Services between South Tottenham and Barking Riverside will be part suspended.
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey for today using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner. For journeys on Monday 26 October and beyond please check back later.
For helpful advice if you need to travel on a rail replacement service, including accessibility and bicycle information, please use our Rail Replacement Services page.
You can find the pick-up and drop-off location of rail replacement services by checking station signage or by searching for your station on our Find a Station page.
Please be advised that replacement vehicles may be busier than usual, and you should allow extra time for your journey.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.
